links.outcome: Hallucinations, inaccuracies, and omissions in AI-generated handoffs versus clinician-authored handoffs
links.effect: Error rates comparable (0.3/handoff both groups); AI errors included inaccuracies (9%) and hallucinations (1%), while clinician handoffs contained only omissions; AI accuracy lower (4.1 vs 4.4, p=0.03).
links.quote: Error rates were comparable (0.3/handoff in both groups); however, AI-generated handoffs included inaccuracies (9% of AI errors) and hallucinations (1% of AI errors), while clinician-authored handoffs contained only omissions.

links.outcome: Quality and safety ratings of AI handoffs versus clinician-authored handoffs
links.effect: Overall quality similar (3.7 vs 3.5, p=0.57); AI higher for completeness (4.1 vs 3.6) and organization (4.4 vs 4.1), lower for conciseness (3.7 vs 4.1) and accuracy (4.1 vs 4.4).
links.quote: Quality ratings were similar between AI and human handoffs (3.7 vs. 3.5, p=0.57).

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of LLM-generated vs. clinician-authored inpatient handoffs assessing quality, safety, and error profiles.
